draft.title: The electromagnetic spectrum
card: The electromagnetic spectrum is the family of electromagnetic waves. In order of increasing frequency: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, x-rays and gamma rays.
All of them travel at the same speed, c, in a vacuum. This is about 3.0 × 10^8 m/s.
Because the speed is fixed at c in a vacuum, a higher frequency means a shorter wavelength. Radio waves have the longest wavelengths and gamma rays the shortest.
The Sun gives out mostly ultraviolet, visible and infrared. The waves differ in frequency and wavelength, not in speed.
draft.remember: One speed in a vacuum, so higher frequency means shorter wavelength.

a.q: Which statement about radio waves and x-rays travelling through a vacuum is correct?
opts: Same speed, and x-rays have the higher frequency
Same speed, and x-rays have the longer wavelength
X-rays travel faster because their frequency is higher
Radio waves travel faster because their wavelength is longer
a.why: All electromagnetic waves travel at c in a vacuum. Since v = fλ, the wave with the higher frequency has the shorter wavelength, so x-rays have the higher frequency. Frequency does not change the speed.
a.clue: Speed is fixed, so what must happen to wavelength when frequency rises?

b.q: Mia compares infrared and ultraviolet waves from the Sun reaching Earth through space. Which comparison is correct?
opts: Ultraviolet has the shorter wavelength, and both travel at c
Ultraviolet has the shorter wavelength and travels faster
Infrared has the shorter wavelength, and both travel at c
Infrared has the shorter wavelength and travels faster
b.why: Ultraviolet has a higher frequency than infrared, so with the same speed c its wavelength is shorter. The tempting idea that higher frequency means faster is wrong, because both travel at c in a vacuum.
b.clue: Place both in the spectrum order, then recall that the speed is the same.

a.best: Same speed, and x-rays have the higher frequency

b.best: Ultraviolet has the shorter wavelength, and both travel at c

problems.detail: The why's reasoning runs backwards. It says the higher-frequency wave has the shorter wavelength, 'so x-rays have the higher frequency', but it never says x-rays have the shorter wavelength. The conclusion does not follow as written. It should say that x-rays are higher in frequency in the spectrum order, so their wavelength is shorter.
